item.title: BNS: foreign currency purchases decreased in the second quarter
item.description: In the second quarter, the Swiss National Bank purchased foreign currencies for 1,4 billion francs, down from the 3,9 billion in the first three months.
item.content:encoded:
## At a Glance - April through June: SNB purchases totaling 1.4 billion francs - Previous quarter: 3.9 billion francs - The SNB will intervene “if necessary” - Statistics published at the end of the following quarter
## Key Facts - Institution → Swiss National Bank (SNB) - Period → April through June - Foreign currency purchases → 1.4 billion francs - First three months of the year → 3.9 billion francs - SNB statement → “if necessary”
### Second-Quarter Data From April to June, the Swiss National Bank (SNB) purchased foreign currencies worth 1.4 billion francs. This volume was lower than the 3.9 billion recorded in the first three months of the year; the comparison thus indicates a decrease in purchases on the foreign exchange market.
The statistics were published at the end of the quarter following the period under review, in accordance with the usual schedule indicated in the source. The data therefore pertains to the second quarter and not to the time of publication. The SNB does not comment on its activities in the foreign exchange market; therefore, the statistics report the amount of foreign currency purchased but do not provide an official rationale for individual transactions.
One clue comes from the latest assessment of the economic and monetary situation. The bank, led by Martin Schlegel, no longer spoke of an “increased willingness” to intervene. Instead, it merely indicated that it would intervene “if necessary.” According to experts, the reason lies in the sharp weakening of the franc. However, this remains the experts’ interpretation, distinct from an official explanation by the SNB.
Foreign exchange transactions are, along with interest rate setting, the main instrument of monetary policy employed by the central bank. For this reason, the number of purchases and the formula used in the assessment must be interpreted together: the former measures the reported volume, while the latter describes the condition specified for a potential intervention. Those who wish to track the franc-euro exchange rate can supplement their analysis with the comparatore CHF/EUR indicator. ## How to interpret the reduction in volume
The comparison between 1,4 and 3,9 billion supports a precise conclusion: in the second quarter, the volume of purchases was lower than in the first three months. On its own, it does not make it possible to quantify the value of the franc, describe an effect on a single person, or attribute to the BNS an objective that the source does not make explicit. This distinction is useful for anyone who lives or works in Switzerland and reads a monetary figure as if it were already a personal forecast.
### Three levels to keep separate
| Level | What the source shows | Limitation of the interpretation | |---|---|---| | Statistical data | Purchases totaling 1,4 billion francs from April to June | Measures the volume of transactions | | Comparison | 3,9 billion in the first three months of the year | Does not by itself quantify the exchange rate | | Interpretation | Experts: marked weakening of the franc | It is not an official comment by the BNS |
The difference in wording in the monetary assessment is a second element to consider. The shift from «increased willingness» to «if necessary» does not amount to an announcement of future purchases or a decision not to intervene. The source merely indicates the condition stated in the assessment. Likewise, the experts' link to the marked weakening of the franc should not be recast as an official explanation, because the BNS does not comment on its own actions in the foreign exchange market.
The reference to interest rates also calls for caution. The source presents foreign-currency operations and interest-rate setting as the main instruments of monetary policy, but does not report an interest-rate decision for the period under consideration. A proper analysis must therefore keep the two instruments separate and not fill the missing information with an assumption.
For those following costo della vita in Svizzera, this is a practical guideline: use the news to follow monetary policy, without turning it into a measure of prices or wages that the source does not provide.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A Reading Procedure
The most reliable way to analyze this news item is to separate the period, amount, comparison, and commentary. This procedure does not require adding external data: simply stick to the categories used in the statistics and monetary analysis.
### A Five-Step Verification
1. Define the period. Start with the words “April through June” and treat them as a fixed time frame. Do not substitute them with the publication date, which falls at the end of the following quarter. 2. Record the amount. Report 1.4 billion francs as the value of the foreign currencies purchased by the SNB during the period. 3. Make the comparison. Compare this figure with the 3.9 billion from the first three months of the year and simply note that the subsequent volume is lower. 4. Check the wording. In the assessment of the economic and monetary situation, note the difference between “increased liquidity” and “if necessary,” without attributing to the SNB an explanation it has not provided. 5. Keep the instruments separate. Consider foreign currency purchases and interest rate setting—identified by the source as the main instruments of monetary policy—together, but do not confuse them.
The fourth check is particularly important: the SNB does not comment on its own actions in the foreign exchange market, while the reference to the significant weakening of the franc is attributed to experts. Maintaining this distinction prevents an interpretation from being presented as a decision by the institution.
The same caution applies to numerical comparisons. The two figures allow for a description of a reduction in volume, but the source does not quantify the exchange rate or indicate an individual effect. A personal worksheet can therefore contain four entries: period, purchases, comparison, and official wording. To complete your balance sheet review, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Analysts rein in their outlook for the Swiss economy
item.description: In Zurich, the index for Swiss economic prospects stands at plus 2,6 points in September, marking a decline compared with August.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Index at +2,6 points in September - 23,1% see an improvement, 20,5% a deterioration - 53,5% expect the SMI to rise - 38,7% see unemployment rising
## Key facts - Indicator → +2,6 points in September - Change from August → -9,5 points - Organizers → UBS and CFA Society Switzerland - Sample → 78 analysts - Survey → 17 and 24 September - Horizon → next six months - Stock market → SMI - Currencies monitored → franc, euro and dollar
In Zurich, the index of Swiss economic prospects stood at +2,6 points in September. The figure, calculated by UBS and CFA Society Switzerland on the basis of a survey of experts from the Swiss financial community, therefore remains in positive territory, but marks a decline of 9,5 points compared with August.
### A still-positive balance
The month's picture is nuanced: the balance remains positive, but optimism has receded. 23,1% of respondents forecast an improvement in economic conditions over the next six months. 20,5% instead expect a deterioration, while 56,4% see no changes. The index is derived from the difference between the first two shares: 23,1 minus 20,5 produces +2,6. The majority oriented towards the status quo does not alter the balance, but reflects a cautious stance in the survey.
Compared with August, the share of optimists fell by 7,2 points. That of pessimists rose by 2,3 points, while analysts favouring the status quo increased by 4,9 points.
### Prices, rates and markets
Regarding inflation, 48,7% of respondents expect Swiss inflation to increase, compared with 5,1% expecting a decrease and 46,2% indicating stability. For short-term interest rates, 61,3% see stability and 36% an increase. Over the long term, the largest group, at 48%, expects no change; 41,3% instead expect an increase.
For the SMI, 53,5% expect an increase over the next six months, 31% stable levels and 15,5% a contraction. The share favouring an increase rose by 4,0 points compared with August. Regarding exchange rates, 44,6% expect the franc to strengthen against the euro, 18,9% a weakening and 36,5% no change. Against the dollar, the respective shares are 44,6%, 18,9% and 29,7%.
The labour market completes the picture: 38,7% expect an increase in unemployment, 58,7% stagnation and 2,7% a decrease.
The survey was conducted on 17 and 24 September and involved 78 analysts. The survey has been conducted since January 2017. Until 2023, CFA Society Switzerland's partner was Credit Suisse; it is now UBS, the bank that acquired its competitor. ## The plus sign is not enough
The +2,6 is not a single verdict on the Swiss economy. It is the result of a balance: expectations of improvement exceed those of deterioration, while the group expecting stability remains the largest. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the most accurate reading is therefore twofold: the general outlook remains positive, but confidence has weakened compared with August.
### Four signals to keep distinct
| Area | Survey signal | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Economic outlook | positive balance, but declining | confidence is present, without uniform enthusiasm | | Inflation | increases and stability remain the main expectations | the cost of living should be monitored, without already considering a price increase a foregone conclusion | | Rates | stability prevails, with expectations of increases | the short and long term do not say the same thing | | SMI | expectations of growth prevail | market expectation, not a guarantee of return | | Employment and exchange rates | stagnation in unemployment and divergent expectations for currencies | signals to follow separately |
For the cost of living, the survey provides an indication of direction but does not quantify the increase in inflation or indicate which expenses would be affected. Those building their budget can complement this reading with the guide on costo della vita in Svizzera, without turning an analysts' forecast into an increase that has already been applied.
The distinction also applies to rates. The largest share expecting stability in the short and long term does not eliminate the group expecting an increase; the message is one of waiting, not of a decision already announced. The same criterion applies to the SMI: the survey provides neither a numerical target nor a guarantee of the result.
As for exchange rates, the euro and dollar should be kept separate. For those who need to monitor the relationship between the franc and the euro, comparatore CHF/EUR helps keep currency analysis distinct from the general reading of the economy. Finally, in employment, the prevalence of stagnation coexists with a significant share expecting unemployment to rise. It is a mixed signal: it does not describe a single person's situation, but suggests not postponing the search for opportunities, while also consulting the annunci di lavoro.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## From reading to action
The survey does not provide an administrative procedure or a decision to apply. The practical use of the data consists of recording the survey date, separating the different indicators, and checking which scenario is being observed. This avoids confusing a financial expectation with a change that has already occurred.
### Five practical steps
1. Set the time horizon. The survey was conducted on 17 and 24 September and looks at the following six months. Note this window before comparing the balance with other data.
2. Separate the balance from the individual variables. Keep economic conditions, inflation, interest rates, SMI, exchange rates and unemployment in separate columns. The positive sign of the index does not mean that all these elements are expected to improve.
3. For the household budget, treat inflation as a scenario. Write down whether the expectation is for an increase, stability or decrease, then compare it with your actual expenses through the guide to costo della vita in Svizzera. Do not attribute an amount to the survey that it does not report.
4. For the exchange rate, indicate the reference currency first. The survey distinguishes expectations for the franc against the euro from those for the franc against the dollar; if you are assessing a conversion into euros, use comparatore CHF/EUR and do not add the two signals.
5. For employment and investments, use two separate checks. You can update your research by consulting annunci di lavoro; for the SMI, instead note the expectation of a rise, stability or contraction without turning it into a promise of returns.
A final check concerns the source of the figures. The 78 analysts belong to the Swiss financial community, the survey has existed since January 2017, and until 2023 the partner of CFA Society Switzerland was Credit Suisse; it is now UBS. These elements describe the survey and help prevent it from being confused with other data.
Among the related content there is also a distinct figure: in Ticino, the increase in health insurance premiums for 2027 is indicated at 3.7%. It is not a component of the index on economic prospects, so it should be kept separate from the reading on inflation, interest rates, the stock market, currencies and unemployment.
To turn these variables into a personal income check, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: KOF revises its growth estimates upward for 2026 and 2027
item.description: KOF at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich revises its estimates: GDP at 1,9% in 2026 and 1,7% in 2027. All details on employment, prices and rates.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - GDP 2026 at 1,9%, versus 0,8% estimated in mid-June - GDP 2027 at 1,7%; 1,7% still forecast for 2028 - Employment 2026 at 1,5%; unemployment at 3,1% - Key rate expected at 0,25% in December
## Key facts - Institute → KOF, Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich - GDP 2026 → 1,9% excluding sporting events; 0,8% estimated in mid-June - GDP 2027 → 1,7%, versus 1,5% estimated previously - GDP 2028 → 1,7% - Employment 2026 → 1,5% - Unemployment → 3,1% in 2026 and 2027; 3% in 2028, indicated as 3,0% - Prices → 0,6% in 2026 and 2027; 0,5% in 2028 - Key rate → 0,25% after the increase expected in December
### The revision of the estimates In the first half of the year, the Swiss economy proved more dynamic than expected. KOF, the institute of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, has therefore revised its growth estimates sharply upwards. The update was reported by Keystone-ATS.
GDP excluding sporting events will grow by 1,9% in 2026, versus 0,8% forecast in mid-June. For 2027, expected growth is 1,7%, that is, 0,2 percentage points above the 1,5% previously indicated. For 2028, the institute offers an initial forecast of 1,7%.
Despite pressure from American trade policy and rising energy prices, the global economy has so far proved resilient. Switzerland also delivered a favorable result: the second quarter brought positive surprises, with export growth concentrated mainly in the pharmaceutical sector.
The expected trajectory will not, however, be uniform. In the third quarter, KOF expects a temporary setback, followed by moderate growth in the fourth quarter of the year. Developments in Germany and the rest of Europe should support the recovery.
The upward revision of the estimates does not erase the pressures already observed: KOF continues to factor both American trade policy and energy into its outlook, while linking the year-end strengthening to the European recovery. The picture therefore remains nuanced, between the positive surprise in the second quarter and the pause expected in the third.
In the labor market, employment should increase by 1,5% in 2026. The unemployment rate is estimated at 3,1% and should remain unchanged in 2027, before falling slightly to 3% in 2028, a figure indicated in the forecast as 3,0%.
Nominal wage growth will continue to slow through 2027. However, contained inflation should allow for slight increases in real earnings. KOF estimates price growth at 0,6% in 2026 and 2027, and then 0,5% in 2028.
For the monetary policy assessment scheduled for December, the Zurich-based institute forecasts a 25-basis-point increase in the key rate, to 0,25%. After that intervention, the rate should remain unchanged for the rest of the forecast horizon. ### Three practical readings For those who live or work in Switzerland, the KOF revision is a trajectory to use for planning, not an outcome already secured. The more favorable annual figure coexists with the expected setback in the third quarter: the sequence of the year matters when assessing employment, wages and expenses.
The first channel is employment. The expected increase in employment in 2026 and the unemployment indicated for 2026 and 2027 describe a picture that KOF still considers resilient, but not uniform. The expected decline in the share of unemployed people in 2028 comes after a year of stability; the practical message is to distinguish annual improvement from when it materializes.
The second channel concerns remuneration. Nominal wages should slow through 2027, while contained inflation should lead to slight increases in real compensation. For costo della vita in Svizzera, therefore, the reading should be made by considering wages and price growth side by side, without confusing a national forecast with the spending of every individual person.
| Indicator | 2026 | 2027 | 2028 | | Price growth | 0,6% | 0,6% | 0,5% | | Unemployment rate | 3,1% | 3,1% | 3% |
The table shows two parallel trends: prices with contained growth and a labor market showing slight improvement only in the final year of the indicated horizon. It is not a promise of individual income, but a reference for interpreting changes from one year to the next.
The third channel is external. The expansion of exports in the second quarter, especially in pharmaceuticals, supports the Swiss picture; pressure from American trade policy and energy pressures nevertheless remain. The recovery of Germany and the rest of Europe is indicated as supporting growth in the fourth part of the year.
Monetary policy also enters the planning, but with a precise step: the assessment scheduled for December. KOF anticipates an increase in the policy rate and then an unchanged parameter for the rest of the horizon. For the reader, this means following the December review separately from the data on prices, wages and employment.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### A four-step process To turn the estimates into concrete monitoring, it is useful to create a sheet updated with each new indication, without adding figures unrelated to those from KOF.
1. Separate the time horizons. Create three distinct rows for 2026, 2027 and 2028. In each, pair GDP growth, employment, unemployment and prices, so as not to mix forecasts for different years.
2. Record employment. Keep the employment figure and the unemployment trajectory separate. Those monitoring the job market can supplement the macro picture by consulting annunci di lavoro, without treating a national estimate as a guarantee for every sector.
3. Distinguish nominal and real. In the sheet, record the expected slowdown in nominal wages through 2027 and, on a separate line, the slight expected increases in real compensation. The comparison prevents reading wage trends without considering price growth.
4. Mark December as a checkpoint. KOF expects the key rate to increase by 25 basis points by then, to 0,25%, followed by stability for the rest of the forecast horizon. After the assessment, the figure can be compared with the initial forecast.
During this review, it is also advisable to keep an eye on the factors indicated by KOF: the recovery in Germany and the rest of Europe, the performance of pharmaceutical exports, and the pressures related to US tariff policy and energy prices. These are factors to monitor together, not items to add automatically to one's personal budget.
The final step is to compare the macroeconomic indications with your own situation, keeping forecasts for the country separate from individual decisions. To translate the wage guidance into your own situation, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: National Council rejects article on earthquakes
item.description: The National Council rejected the constitutional article on earthquake damage to properties: responsibility remains with private owners.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 99 opposed, 84 in favor and 8 abstentions in the National Council. - The Confederation will not have the authority to finance repairs. - The CAPTE-N proposal indicated 0.5% of the insured amount. - The Federal Council's message provided for 0.7%.
## Key facts - Decision → constitutional article rejected - CAPTE-N proposal → 0.5% of the insured amount - Federal message → 0.7% - Owners with a policy → 15% - Coverage according to Jon Pult → 80% without coverage
99 votes against, 84 in favor and 8 abstentions: today the National Council rejected the constitutional article that would have given the Confederation the authority to finance the repair of buildings after major earthquakes. The vote closes the dossier: following the Council of States' previous decision not to consider the matter, this is the second negative decision and the matter has been definitively shelved.
The proposal put forward by the majority of the Committee for the Environment, Spatial Planning and Energy, CAPTE-N, provided for a solidarity mechanism. In the event of a major earthquake, a contribution would have been levied on property owners amounting to 0.5% of the insured amount. It was a different solution from the Federal Council's message, which indicated 0.7%; the latter had already been rejected by the Council of States last December.
### Positions expressed in the chamber
Stefan Müller-Altermatt, Centre/SO, defended the proposal on behalf of the committee majority. He recalled that there is currently no constitutional provision for such cases and that the burden remains with the owners. According to his account, only 15% of owners have taken out a policy, and the primary responsibility will continue to fall on them. The committee had taken as its extreme case an earthquake of an intensity expected to recur approximately once every hundred years.
Jon Pult, SP/GR, instead accused the sector lobby of confusing the insurability of properties with their actual coverage, arguing that 80% lack it. The minority, represented by Christian Wasserfallen, FDP/BE, pointed to the difference between the damage caused by an earthquake in an urban center and that in a rural area, as well as the uncertainty over who should accurately calculate the total damage.
Michael Graber, a Swiss People's Party member from VS, also believed that the legislation would have penalized those who had voluntarily chosen to protect themselves. This position prevailed. Keystone-ATS's report thus records the project's definitive end. ## What changes in practical terms
The 0,5% was not approved: it was CAPTE-N's proposal, calculated on the insured sum. The 0,7%, on the other hand, was provided for in the Federal Council's dispatch, already rejected by the Council of States. The final rejection of the matter closes both hypotheses without establishing the solidarity mechanism under discussion.
The practical result described in the debate is that the absence of a constitutional provision for these cases remains and owners retain primary responsibility. The issue was also presented as a distinction between insurability and actual coverage. Jon Pult accused the industry lobby of confusing the two concepts; Stefan Müller-Altermatt recalled that only 15% of owners have taken out an insurance policy. Pult added that 80% have none. The source reports the two percentages through different parliamentary interventions, linking them to the discussion about the degree of protection afforded to properties.
### The crux of the differences between cantons
The minority position indicated why the project was considered uncertain. Christian Wasserfallen observed that an earthquake in an urban center would cause much greater damage than one in a rural area. He also pointed out that it is unclear who should determine the total amount of damage precisely. Added to this is the fact that several cantons do not have mandatory insurance for properties.
For the owner, therefore, the concrete fact is not a new percentage to apply, but the continuation of the primary responsibility indicated in the chamber. The source does not describe a shift toward federal financing of repairs: it describes a rejected proposal and the continuation of the situation referred to by the parliamentarians.

Michael Graber, a member of the Swiss People's Party from VS, had argued that a law would have penalized those who had voluntarily chosen to take precautions against the risk. His position prevailed together with the minority's objections, which considered the absence of legislation preferable to ineffective legislation. The vote leaves the issues of coverage, damage assessment and differences between cantons open in the federal debate.

The source does not describe a new federal procedure for requesting financing for repairs. The most concrete way to read the decision is to separate four elements.
1. Competence. The vote concerned the Confederation's ability to finance the repair of buildings after severe earthquakes. The constitutional article was not approved, so primary responsibility remains with the owners.
2. Percentages. The 0.5% was CAPTE-N's proposal based on the insured sum; the 0.7% appeared in the Federal Council's dispatch. The former remained in the rejected bill, while the latter had already been rejected by the Council of States.

For anyone who owns a property, the correct reading is not to look for a new percentage to apply: the vote rejected the measure. item.title: Health insurance premiums: discounts for foregoing end-of-life treatments
item.description: Tilman Slembeck proposes lower premiums for those who voluntarily give up life-prolonging therapies in the terminal phase.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Slembeck proposes reduced premiums for those who forgo end-of-life treatments. - The idea comes after yet another premium increase. - Three factors drive costs: demographics, technology and demand. - The model would be voluntary and individual.
## Key facts - Proponent → Tilman Slembeck, healthcare expert and economist - Institutions → ZHAW, University of St. Gallen, Confederation and cantons - Source → interview with NZZ after the premium increase - Proposal → more affordable premiums in exchange for forgoing therapies - Costs → demographics, medical-technological progress and maximum care - Scope → life-prolonging therapies at the terminal stage
Tilman Slembeck, a healthcare-sector expert and professor of economics at ZHAW, the Zurich University of Applied Sciences, has proposed lower premiums for those who voluntarily forgo life-prolonging therapies at the terminal stage. The idea was outlined in an interview published by Neue Zürcher Zeitung (NZZ) following yet another premium increase.
Slembeck also teaches at the University of St. Gallen and has followed the sector for years, advising the Confederation and the cantons. His thesis is that the Swiss healthcare system has not yet reached its limit: it is designed to expand and resembles a self-service store. People continue to pay their own premiums, while the state eases the burden on more than a third of low-income families through premium subsidies worth billions.
> “The pain threshold is still far from being reached,” the academic argues.
The cost argument starts from three elements. Demographics weigh heavily because the population is aging and the baby-boom generation is entering an age in which it makes more frequent use of medical services. Medical-technological progress makes more effective treatments available, including those in cancer therapy, but also very costly ones. Finally, those who pay premiums for years expect the maximum level of care when they need it and do not want to give anything up.
### The limit on care, according to the expert
The most delicate point concerns the end of life and the relationship with cassa malati. Treatments can become very costly, and Slembeck doubts that it is possible to set a collective limit accepted by everyone. Even within a family, he observes, it is difficult to decide whether to adopt life-prolonging measures and which ones to choose. Cost-driven rationing seems to him almost impossible to accept at the social level.
The proposed approach shifts the level at which the decision is made: the insured person voluntarily forgoes life-prolonging therapies at the terminal stage and receives more affordable premiums in exchange. Slembeck considers this individual self-rationing feasible in principle. The proposal is linked to his idea of healthcare networks beyond cantonal borders, competing with one another and based on flat-rate amounts per insured person. ## What would change for the insured person
For the reader, the practical point is not an already quantified discount, but the mechanism being considered. The reduction in premiums would be linked to a specific renunciation: not using life-prolonging therapies when the condition has reached its terminal stage. The financial benefit, therefore, would not be separate from the healthcare decision, but would be the trade-off for it.
### Two levels of decision-making
| Level | Description in the source | Hypothesized effect | |---|---|---| | Collective | Limit on care decided for society | Difficult consensus on rationing for cost reasons | | Individual | Voluntary renunciation by the insured person | More affordable premiums and self-rationing |
In the first scheme, the limit would concern society as a whole and would require social agreement. In the second, the decision would remain with the person who chooses to join the model. It is this shift that makes the idea different from a generalized cut in benefits: the incentive is not imposed on everyone, but would accompany an explicit renunciation by the individual.
The trade-off is stark. Anyone who pays premiums for years tends to expect maximum coverage when they need it; the imagined model instead asks them to accept foregoing those therapies precisely in the terminal phase, in exchange for more affordable premiums. The source does not indicate the amount of the discount, the enrollment formula or a start date. It therefore does not make it possible to estimate the savings or determine which insured persons would fall under the model.
### Which part of the costs would be affected
The proposal would act on the willingness to give something up, not on the aging of the population or the price of new treatments. In other words, it would intervene on the third factor identified by Slembeck, leaving the other two unchanged. This is also why the issue enters costo della vita as a choice between lower recurring expenditure and a voluntary limitation of future care, not as a general solution to rising costs.
The organizational dimension remains national and cantonal. The healthcare networks envisioned by Slembeck would have to cross cantonal borders, compete with one another and operate with lump-sum amounts per insured person. The model of more affordable premiums fits into the same logic: if no one wants to give anything up, the financial incentive would become the lever for curbing growth.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read the proposal and follow its developments
Anyone who wants to assess the idea can start from a simple distinction: the source describes a model suggested by the expert, not a process to be activated for insured persons. The conditional formulas used in the text indicate a hypothesis. This avoids turning the benefit described into an already available right or looking for a deadline that the source does not indicate.
### A five-step check
1. Define the scope. The waiver concerns life-prolonging therapies in the terminal phase. It should not be extended to every medical treatment or every choice concerning premiums: the connection described is between a specific decision and more affordable premiums.
2. Separate the objective from the instrument. The objective is to ease the growth of health insurers' costs; the instrument hypothesized is individual self-rationing supported by a financial incentive. Keeping the two levels distinct prevents presenting the discount as a general reform.
3. Verify who decides. The text contrasts the collective limit, which is difficult to share for cost reasons, with the individual's voluntary choice. This is the question to use when reading any possible development: is the decision proposed for everyone or only for those who opt in?
4. Isolate the spending factors. Demography, medical and technological progress, and demand for the highest level of care play different roles in Slembeck's reasoning. The proposal concerns only the willingness to waive treatment; it does not replace analysis of the other two factors.
5. Consider the organizational dimension. Slembeck links the issue to healthcare networks extending beyond cantonal borders, competing with one another and capable of working with lump-sum amounts per insured person. The Confederation and the Cantons are already identified in the source as stakeholders whom the expert has been advising for years.
For a responsible reading, it is advisable to separate what is described from what still needs to be defined: the amount of the premium, the method of enrollment, and practical implementation are not set out in the text. There is no need for estimates based on missing data. Instead, it is important to keep clear the link between individual choice and financial incentive, which is the heart of the proposal.

item.title: Cap on psychotherapists covered by health insurance
item.description: Lorenzo Quadri presents a motion to introduce a cantonal cap on psychological psychotherapists because of the increase in AOMS expenditure.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Quadri calls for a cap on psychological psychotherapists - The change came into force on 1 luglio 2022 - ZSR facilities grew by 120% - AOMS expenditure reached 922 million in 2024
## Key facts - Proposal → cantonal cap for psychological psychotherapists - Presenter → Lorenzo Quadri (Lega) - Billing → AOMS on medical prescription from 1 luglio 2022 - Facilities with active ZSR → 2'437 in the third quarter of 2022; 5'374 in the second quarter of 2024 - AOMS costs → 528 million francs in 2021; 922 million in 2024 - Cited legal basis → Article 55a of the LAMal
### The request to the Federal Council On 1 luglio 2022, psychological psychotherapists obtained the possibility of billing compulsory health-care insurance (AOMS) directly, on the basis of a medical prescription. This change is the starting point for the motion submitted to the Federal Council by National Councillor Lorenzo Quadri (Lega).
The text calls for the Cantons to be allowed to set a cap on the number of psychological psychotherapists authorized to bill their services to compulsory health insurance. For Quadri, the sector should have an instrument analogous to that already provided by the LAMal for doctors. Within the LAMal e cassa malati system, the text therefore focuses the request on the number of persons authorized to bill AOMS; the source describes the medical prescription as the basis of the regime that came into force in 2022.
The numerical comparison is at the heart of the motion. Between 2022 and 2025, specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy increased from 3'974 to 4'141, an increase of 4,2%. During the same period, specialists in child and adolescent psychiatry and psychotherapy rose from 742 to 772, equal to 4%. Psychological psychotherapy facilities with an active ZSR number, on the other hand, increased from 2'437 in the third quarter of 2022 to 5'374 in the second quarter of 2024: more than 120% higher.
Quadri also cites expenditure recorded by Obsan. The costs of psychological psychotherapy covered by AOMS increased from 528 million francs in 2021 to 922 million in 2024, with average annual growth of 20,4%.
The institutional reference is Article 55a of the LAMal. Today, according to the National Councillor, the Cantons can set maximum numbers for doctors in certain specialties, but they do not have an analogous instrument for psychological psychotherapists. The request brought to Bern aims precisely to bridge this difference.
The source thus presents a political request: the growth in facilities, the increase in expenditure and the difference between doctors and psychological psychotherapists are used to support extending quota restrictions to the Cantons. ## Practical implications for cantons and policyholders
### The case of Ticino
The territorial focus identified in the motion is Ticino. According to Quadri, the canton has seen a significant increase in Italian professionals, a consequence of the free movement of people. The national councillor adds that the canton’s per-capita use of psychotherapeutic services exceeds the Swiss average by more than 50%. Quadri presents this percentage as a figure that should raise questions about the actual appropriateness of all therapies.
For a canton, the request would have a precise administrative consequence: the ability to set a maximum number of professionals authorized to bill AOMS, as is already the case for doctors. For anyone using a service under the regime described, the practical distinction would be between the medical prescription, identified as the basis for direct billing, and any authorization within the cantonal cap requested by the motion. The first element stems from the 2022 change; the second is the extension Quadri wants to obtain.
### Work and disability pensions
The motion also links the surge in prescriptions to absences from work and the related costs for the economy. The issue is presented not only as an AOMS expenditure item, but also as a matter with economic consequences linked to absences from work. This is the practical point for anyone following costo della vita in Svizzera: the debate puts both the rise in healthcare costs and the economic consequences of absences on the table.
The second connection concerns disability pensions among young people. In 2025, Quadri writes, approximately 2'800 new disability pensions were awarded to people aged 18 to 24; approximately 70% would be attributable to mental disorders. The national councillor uses this figure to argue that developments in the sector require more urgent action.
> “It is necessary to ask whether all these new pensions are truly justified,” Quadri says.
The text juxtaposes these figures with the discussion of the rise in prescriptions and absences from work, as arguments in support of intervention in the sector.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to orient yourself before billing
### Four concrete steps
The verification can begin with the professional category. The source distinguishes specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy, those specializing in childhood and adolescence, and psychological psychotherapists. This distinction avoids confusing the increase in specialists with that of facilities with an active ZSR number.
- First: place the service in time. The date to mark is 1 July 2022, the date on which psychological psychotherapists obtained the possibility of billing the AOMS directly. - Second: verify the prerequisite indicated by the source. Under the regime described, direct billing to mandatory health care insurance takes place on the basis of a medical prescription. - Third: separate the number of ZSR facilities from the number of specialists. These are quantities used in the motion to describe different phenomena and should not be added together. - Fourth: distinguish the rule described from the policy proposal. Quotas for physicians are already provided for by Article 55a of the LAMal; for psychological psychotherapists, the motion asks the Cantons for an analogous instrument.
### If the request were accepted
The scenario to follow would be the possible cantonal authorization to bill the AOMS within a maximum number. Practical verification would therefore remain anchored to the professional's category, the medical prescription, and the possibility of billing within the framework decided by the Cantons. The available text describes a motion addressed to the Federal Council: Quadri's request must not be turned into a rule already in force.

item.title: University: equal tuition fees for Swiss and EU students
item.description: The Council of States approves equal treatment for Swiss and EU students. The Confederation should cover the Cantons' lost revenue for four years.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States approves equal treatment for Swiss and EU students - Two polytechnics: from 730 to 2.190 CHF per semester - The Confederation should cover the bill for four years - For students from third countries, fees at least three times higher
## Key facts - Decision → Council of States - Rule → same fee for Swiss and EU citizens - Example from 2025 → from 730 to 2.190 CHF per semester - Coverage → Confederation for four years - Third countries → at least three times the Swiss fee
### The Bern vote The Council of States approved on Wednesday the amendments to the law introducing equal treatment between Swiss students and citizens of the European Union. The decision concerns university fees and follows the outcome of negotiations between Bern and Brussels. For those arriving from the EU, the principle stated is clear: studying in Switzerland must not cost more than it does for a Swiss student.
The rule does not concern universities alone. The text provides that Swiss universities of applied sciences should also return to applying the same fees to the two groups. The return to the same fee comes after a period during which several universities had increased tuition fees, but the amount indicated by the source remains an example referring to the two federal institutes of technology.
The increase had a precise financial reason. Several Swiss universities had raised their fees to cope with growing deficits, while cuts to federal contributions are planned from 2027. The clearest example concerns the two federal institutes of technology: from 2025, they tripled fees for foreign students, raising them from 730 to 2.190 francs per semester.
Under the new arrangement, the bill for the lower revenues should be assumed by the Confederation. Full coverage is planned for four years for the Cantons concerned and their universities. For the reader who is calculating the costo della vita in Svizzera, the decisive distinction is therefore between Swiss or EU citizenship and coming from a third country.
The rule for the latter group remains different: fees will have to continue to be at least three times higher than those applied to Swiss students. The vote in the Council of States thus establishes a clear separation between equal treatment for Swiss and EU citizens and distinct treatment for students from third countries. The negotiating package therefore changes the situation compared with the period of increases: on the one hand, equal treatment; on the other, a different threshold for those arriving from third countries. ## The difference between the categories
### The comparison that matters The practical effect of the vote can be understood by comparing the categories indicated in the text. It is therefore not enough to focus on the word foreigner, used to describe the increase at the two federal institutes of technology from 2025: the new negotiated package distinguishes EU citizens from students coming from third countries. For a family planning studies in Switzerland, the first check is the category applied to the fee.
| Category | Treatment indicated | | Swiss students | basis of comparison for fees | | EU citizens | same fee as Swiss students | | Students from third countries | at least three times the fee for Swiss students | | Two federal institutes of technology, from 2025 | fees from 730 to 2.190 CHF per semester |
The table does not authorize turning 2.190 francs into a general rate. The source presents that figure as an example referring to the two federal institutes of technology and links it to foreign students. The negotiated rule, however, has a broader scope: universities and universities of applied sciences will have to apply equal treatment to Swiss and EU citizens.
The party absorbing the financial effect also changes. The student sees the rule on the fee; the affected cantons and their universities face lower revenues, which the Confederation should cover in full for four years. This separates the price charged to the student from the public compensation mechanism described in the source. The cuts to federal contributions planned from 2027 remain the reason why the higher education institutions had sought additional revenue, but the new negotiated package changes the framework.
The operational point, therefore, is not to automatically apply the latest available amount, but to read the institution, category and period indicated together. The source provides a rule of equal treatment and an example of an increase; it does not present a single fee schedule for all institutions.
For a personal assessment, it is advisable to keep three figures separate: the fee charged by the institution, the Swiss reference figure and, only for third countries, the threshold of at least three times that amount. Anyone who needs to compare amounts expressed in francs with a family budget can place the comparatore CHF/EUR alongside them, without confusing currency conversion with the rule of equal treatment. The text focuses the measure on university fees.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to carry out the check
### Three steps before the budget The new approach can be translated into a practical check without adding rules that the source does not indicate. The first step is to identify the type of institution: equal treatment applies to Swiss universities and universities of applied sciences. The second is to place the student in the correct category: Swiss citizen, EU citizen or person from a third country.
The third step is to use the right reference point. For Swiss and EU citizens, the fee must be the same. For third countries, the principle remains that the fee must be at least three times higher than the Swiss one. If the comparison starts from the example of the two federal institutes of technology, both figures must be noted: 730 francs per semester before the indicated increase and 2.190 francs from 2025. This figure serves to interpret the increase cited by the source, not to replace the fee charged by each university.
### Separating tuition and funding The fourth check concerns public funding. The four years of full coverage described in the negotiating package concern the lower revenues of the affected Cantons and their universities. In the individual budget, this figure must be kept separate from tuition: the source presents the Confederation as the entity that should cover the bill, not as an item to be added to the student's payment.
A separate check helps avoid mixing different aspects. The increase at the two federal institutes of technology is linked to growing deficits and cuts to federal contributions planned from 2027; equal treatment for EU citizens, on the other hand, derives from the new negotiating package with Brussels, approved by the Council of States. They are two elements of the same matter, but not the same calculation.
Anyone preparing an estimate can finally list on a single sheet the institution, student category, stated semester fee and comparison with the Swiss rate. To compare study-related expenses with overall financial resources, the final step is to use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.description: In the first nine months, the Institute for Young Entrepreneurs recorded 41'716 new companies in Switzerland. Ticino leads the ranking with growth of 9,3%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 41'716 new registrations in the first nine months - New business formations in Ticino: growth of 9,3% - Consulting leads with 4'307 registrations - IT rises by one fifth
## Key facts - Period → first nine months - New companies registered → 41'716 - Growth over the same period of the previous year → 2,1% - Growth compared with the average of the last five years → almost 6% - Leading region → Ticino, growth of 9,3%
### A record concentrated in the first nine months
41'716 new companies were registered for the first time in the Swiss commercial register in the first nine months of the year. The result represents a record and corresponds to growth of 2,1% compared with the same period of the previous year. The comparison with the average of the last five years also indicates an increase of almost 6%. The data was reported by the Institute for Young Entrepreneurs (IFJ), in a survey published on Wednesday.
The record is not distributed evenly among the major regions. Ticino leads the ranking with growth of 9,3%. It is followed by Northwestern Switzerland, at 4,3%, Espace Mittelland, at 3%, Eastern Switzerland, at 2,6%, Central Switzerland, at 2,4%, and Southwestern Switzerland, at 0,5%. Zurich is the only area indicated with a negative change: new formations recorded a decline of 0,3%.
The source also points to a broad distribution among sectors. Consulting ranks first with 4'307 new registrations, ahead of crafts, with 4'041, and real estate, with 3'683. The Information Technology and Communication Technologies sector stands out for its pace of growth: formations increased by one fifth compared with the previous year and reached 3'508.
The picture therefore combines two elements: the national high in new registrations and a marked difference between the areas considered. Ticino records the strongest change among the major regions listed, while Zurich is the only one to record a decline. At the sectoral level, consulting's first place comes ahead of craft, real estate and technology activities. These are the data highlighted by the IFJ analysis of the first nine months.
The scope of the comparison remains that stated by the survey: newly registered companies and the first nine months. The growth of 2,1% compares the same period of the previous year, while the almost 6% uses the average of the last five years as a reference. These are therefore three different measures of the same phenomenon: the total registered, the year-on-year comparison and the comparison with the average. The geographical analysis adds a fourth level, that of the major regions. ## What the regional comparison shows
The national record should be read along two axes: geography and activity. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the distinction helps prevent confusing a regional percentage with a measure of the entire country, or the numerical lead of one sector with the growth rate of another.

item.description: The Council of States votes today on the referendum for Bilaterals III, while the National Council examines federal properties for 2026.

## In brief - The Council of States votes on the type of referendum on Bilaterals III - Wage protections and immigration clause at stake - The National Council examines 773,8 million for federal properties 2026 - Agenda also includes the army, earthquakes, heatwaves and drought
## Key facts - Place → Bern - Dossier → Bilaterals III - Referendum → optional or mandatory - Civilian properties of the Confederation 2026 → 773,8 million Swiss francs - Swiss National Library → 211,7 million Swiss francs - Swiss Embassy in London → 96 million Swiss francs - Earthquake project → levy of up to 0,7% of the insured value of buildings - Other parliamentary business → Army financing; Heatwaves and drought
In Bern, the Council of States has reached the third day of debates on Bilaterals III. After some decisions have already been made, the session is devoted to the vote on the decisive question of the referendum for the new agreements with Brussels.
The first point of contention concerns the procedure: the optional referendum requires only a majority of the people, while the mandatory referendum requires a majority of the people and the cantons. The Council of States must also express its views on the wage protection provisions, which provide protection against dismissal for employee representatives. For the left, this is a condition for supporting the new bilateral agreements. The cantonal chamber is finally called upon to vote on approval of the entire package of agreements.
### Decisions already passed and the second federal front
In the previous days, yesterday and Monday, the Council of States had agreed to supplement the safeguard clause with an incentive tax. The clause would be activated to limit excessive immigration causing serious economic and social problems. The Council of States also approved the creation in Switzerland of an independent authority to oversee state aid, separate from Comco. The mechanism is required by the EU to prevent distortions of competition in its internal market.
In parallel, the National Council is beginning its examination of the dispatch on the Confederation's civilian properties for 2026, with planned expenditure of 773,8 million Swiss francs. The largest project announced is the renovation and expansion of the Swiss National Library in Bern, headquarters of the Federal Office of Culture, for 211,7 million. The complete renovation of the Swiss Embassy in London is also planned, after more than 50 years of operation, for 96 million.
The People's Chamber must then address the mandatory contribution from property owners to a fund to repair earthquake damage. The new legislation would require a constitutional amendment and would allow the Confederation to levy up to 0,7 per cent of the insured value of buildings. The agenda finally includes the extraordinary session on army financing and the debate on heatwaves and drought, with interpellations addressed to the Federal Council. ## From voting to concrete impact
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the session brings together dossiers with different paths. The referendum concerns the required majority; wage protections concern the protection of employee representatives; the earthquake project concerns property owners; the heatwave concerns questions to the Federal Council. Keeping these aspects separate prevents a measure still under consideration from being read as already implemented.
### Four dossiers, four points to check
| Dossier | Concrete element | Indicated status | |---|---|---| | Referendum on Bilaterals III | Majority of the people or of the people and Cantons | Vote expected in the Council of States | | Wage protections | Protection against dismissal of employee representatives | Vote expected in the Council of States | | Safeguard clause | Incentive tax to limit excessive immigration | Accepted by the Council of States | | State aid | Authority independent of Comco | Approved by the Council of States |
The first practical point is the difference between the two referendums. Under the optional model, the decision is made by a majority of the people; under the mandatory model, the Cantons are also included. For anyone following a possible national vote, these are therefore not two equivalent formulas: the set of required majorities changes.
The wage dossier should be read carefully. The parliamentary text referred to concerns protection against the dismissal of employee representatives. The left makes this a condition for supporting the new bilateral agreements. To relate this issue to one’s own employment situation, one can consult busta paga svizzera, while keeping separate the content of one’s own salary and the protection discussed by the Council of States.
The safeguard clause links the incentive tax to limiting excessive immigration when this is the cause of serious economic and social problems. The state aid authority, on the other hand, oversees competition in the EU internal market and is described as separate from Comco. For a complementary look at everyday expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera is available, without confusing it with the specific content of the parliamentary decisions.
For property owners, the decisive point is the status of the process: in the first reading, the Council of States rejected the project, while the preparatory committee of the National Council proposes approving it. The contribution would be mandatory and could reach 0,7% of the insured value of the buildings, but the new legislation would require a constitutional amendment. The dossier should therefore not be confused with expenditure on the Confederation’s civilian properties, which belongs to a separate message for 2026.
The debate on heatwaves and drought also has a different nature: the interpellations ask the Federal Council how it intends to address the effects of the two phenomena. These are therefore questions addressed to the Government, alongside the special session on army financing, not a practical measure described in the text.

When a parliamentary day includes several measures, the most practical way is to associate each question with the competent body and the type of decision. The following grid uses only the steps indicated for the Council of States and the National Council.
### Four operational steps
1. For Bilaterals III, first check which of the two referendums the Council of States chooses. Optional means a majority of the people; mandatory means a majority of the people and the cantons. Only after this step should the vote on approving the package of agreements be considered.
2. For wage protections, look for the precise reference to protection against the dismissal of staff representatives. This is the point indicated as the left's condition for supporting the new bilateral agreements. It should not be replaced with a generic reference to wages: the topic described is the protection of representatives.
3. For the property dossier, separate the dispatch on the Confederation's civilian properties from the project on the earthquake fund. The former concerns 2026 expenditure, including the works announced in Bern and London. The latter concerns a mandatory contribution by owners, of up to 0,7% of the insured value of the buildings, and requires a constitutional amendment. To follow the parliamentary procedure, also note the divergence between the Council of States' rejection at first reading and the favorable proposal of the National Council's preparatory committee.
4. For the other agenda items, distinguish a special session from a current-affairs debate. Army funding belongs to the first category; heatwaves and drought to the second. In the latter case, the interpellations ask the Federal Council how to address the effects of the phenomena. This distinction prevents attributing a decision already taken to the interpellations.
The same caution applies to the safeguard clause and to the authority on state aid: the former was completed with an incentive tax, the latter was approved as an authority independent of Comco. item.description: Analysis of healthcare costs: the average premium in Ticino reaches 519,90 francs in 2027. Comparisons, efficiency and OECD data compared.

## In brief - OECD: life expectancy in Switzerland at 84,3 years - Healthcare prices: 52% above the OECD average - Prevention: 1,9% of spending versus 3,4% for the OECD - Average premium in Ticino in 2027: 519,90 francs
## Key facts - Life expectancy in Switzerland → 84,3 years - Swiss healthcare prices → 52% above the average of OECD countries - Prevention → 1,9% of healthcare spending; OECD average 3,4% - Average monthly premium in Ticino in 2027 → 519,90 francs - Average monthly premium in Zug → approximately 276,20 francs
For 2027, the average monthly premium in Ticino is given as 519,90 francs, compared with a Swiss average of approximately 412 francs. Ticino therefore remains the canton with the highest average premium. In Zug, the stated amount is instead approximately 276,20 francs per month. The comparison makes visible a difference between cantons that the national average alone does not show.
The analysis by Corrado Amato starts with this question: an effective healthcare system must guarantee quality care, accessibility and safety, but also use resources in a transparent and responsible manner. To place the premium in the context of day-to-day finances, the topic is also linked to costo della vita in Svizzera.
### Health outcomes and spending
The OECD reports a life expectancy of 84,3 years for Switzerland, population coverage for an essential set of services, and a very low level of unmet healthcare needs. The source considers these results important: the issue is not presented as a lack of quality of care per se, but as the need to understand why the system costs so much.
The Commonwealth Fund's international comparison examines ten high-income countries across access to care, quality, administrative efficiency, equity and health outcomes. Australia, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom rank highest overall, with no country excelling in every area. Australia combines universal coverage, a public system and a private component; the Netherlands entrust compulsory insurance to highly regulated private insurers and give primary care a central role; France has a strong collective component in financing.
The comparison, therefore, is not intended to proclaim a better model. It shows that universal healthcare can be organized in different ways and that some countries manage to contain spending more effectively without foregoing protection for the population. ## From price to value
For those who pay, the Swiss average is a reference, not a complete answer. The comparison between Ticino, the Swiss average and Zug shows that the interpretation of the premium must remain linked to the territory. It does not, on its own, say why the difference exists and does not authorize turning an amount into an automatic judgment about the quality of care.
### Three questions for reading the data
| Point | Question | |---|---| | Spending | How much does the average monthly premium cost in the chosen reference? | | Results | What does the system deliver in terms of life expectancy, coverage and unmet needs? | | Efficiency | Where do signals emerge that warrant discussion, such as prevention and generic drugs? |
This distinction avoids two opposite errors. The first is to stop at the price and conclude that high spending automatically amounts to waste. The OECD indicates that prices of health goods and services in Switzerland are 52% above the average for OECD countries, but the source specifies that the figure alone does not demonstrate the presence of waste. Wages, the cost of living, the organization of care and the structure of the system all have an impact.
The second error is to consider good health outcomes sufficient. The share allocated to prevention is 1,9% of health spending, compared with 3,4% of the OECD average, while the share of generic drugs on the market is much lower than the OECD average. These are areas for discussion, not a ready-made solution: the source says that these indicators alone do not make it possible to point to an answer.
### A methodological choice
For a responsible health policy, the practical outcome is to balance population protection with spending containment. Asking citizens to pay more cannot be the only step. The comparison between Australia, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and France suggests examining organization, financing and access without seeking a model to copy in its entirety. To complement the general reading with a review of premiums, one can use confrontatore LAMal/cassa malati.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## A practical path
The source makes it possible to build an orderly assessment without choosing a solution in advance. The goal is to relate the premium, results and efficiency indicators, keeping the observed data separate from the questions that arise from them.
### Five steps
1. Start with the year. Write 2027 at the top of the comparison and indicate that the figure concerns an average monthly premium. 2. Put the references side by side. Report 519,90 francs for Ticino, around 412 for the Swiss average and around 276,20 for Zug. 3. Place the outcomes alongside them. Add a life expectancy of 84,3 years, coverage for an essential set of services and the very low level of unmet healthcare needs recorded by the OECD. 4. Check efficiency. Mark 52% for healthcare prices, then distinguish prevention at 1,9% from the OECD average of 3,4% and the lowest share of generic medicines. 5. Compare the models. Use Australia, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and France to formulate questions about access, financing and organization, not to automatically choose a winner.
Once the grid is complete, the reading can follow multiple scenarios. If one starts from the result, one looks at life expectancy, coverage and unmet needs; if one starts from the cost, one looks at prices and the gap between territorial benchmarks. If one is seeking efficiency, one examines prevention and generics. The three perspectives do not give the same answer, but they prevent using a single indicator to judge the entire system.
The final step consists in turning the data into questions: what elements explain the higher spending? What room for improvement deserves discussion? What protection do we want to guarantee? The source does not offer a single answer and reminds us that no country excels in every sector. The comparison therefore serves to guide the debate, not to automatically import a foreign model.

Peter Füglistaler, former director of the Federal Office of Transport (FOT), admitted in an interview published today by the Basler Zeitung that he made mistakes in the expansion of the Swiss railway network. His self-criticism concerns the relationship between planning and implementation: in his view, Switzerland plans, but hardly builds anymore.
### The example of the Basel S-Bahn
The case cited is the Basel S-Bahn. Füglistaler considers it over-engineered, without a clear timeline or financial horizon. The search for the perfect solution slowed down the implementation: the system, according to his reconstruction, lost sight of when to start building.

This passage highlights the complexity of the interaction between the Confederation, the Cantons, and the SBB. Füglistaler admitted to having been part of this system.

On that occasion, he advocated for a gradual implementation rather than the systematic pursuit of the perfect solution.
The statements are part of the debate on the strengthening of infrastructure under Transport '45. ## In brief - No federal minimum wage; some cantons provide for one. - Maximum working hours: 45 or 50 hours per week. - AVS/AI/IPG: 5.3% paid by the employee. - Vacation: at least 4 weeks; 5 under 20.

## The starting point for Vaud
In Switzerland there is no federal minimum wage: some cantons do, however, have their own threshold. For anyone looking for or changing jobs in the Canton of Vaud, this is the first check to make, before assigning a salary level applicable to everyone to a training course or a sector. There is no single national figure: the comparison starts with the potentially applicable cantonal rule, the contract and any relevant collective agreement.
### Looking beyond the figure in the offer
The second concrete piece of information is working hours. The maximum limit is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and retail; in other sectors it reaches 50 hours. The difference affects how an offer is read because the same gross amount must be linked to the working time specified in the contract. The minimum vacation entitlement is four weeks, rising to five for anyone under 20. Notice periods are one, two or three months: one month in the first year, two from the second to the ninth and three from the tenth.
Contributions then come into play in relation to salary. AVS/AI/IPG amounts to 5.3% for the employee, while the total with the employer reaches 10.6%. AD/AC is 1.1% up to the annual maximum; LAINF/LAA ranges from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. For LPP/BVG on the coordinated salary, the rates indicated are 7% between 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from age 55 up to reference age.
These items do not include LAMal/KVG. It is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival; it is private insurance with per-capita premiums, not a tax or a salary contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region, while premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. To check the transition from gross to net, you can consult busta paga svizzera, without turning a health insurance premium into a salary deduction. ## Net pay also depends on taxes and housing
A salary comparison in Canton Vaud does not end with gross pay and payroll deductions. The cost of living also depends on the municipality, the LAMal premium and rent. Swiss taxation has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax.
### Do not confuse the offices
Distinguishing responsibilities avoids using the wrong data to estimate net pay. The AFC/ESTV handles the IFD and IVA. Cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AI/LPP, but does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set tax rates. Therefore, a salary statistic is not a tax table, and a reference to social security does not replace the calculation of direct federal tax.
| Item | Rule to keep separate | What to check | |---|---|---| | Taxes | three levels | federal, cantonal and municipal | | LAMal/KVG | per-capita premium | canton or region and premium reduction | | Rent | maximum deposit of three months | blocked account in the tenant's name | | Contract | employment rules | sector, working hours, holidays and termination |
A hypothetical worker evaluating two offers with the same gross pay must therefore compare the items in the same order, without adding LAMal to salary contributions. The health insurance premium remains separate; taxation changes with the three levels and the municipality; housing may require a deposit, but the limit is three months' rent and the account is in the tenant's name. Tenancy law is federal and the same in every canton. If the landlord gives notice, the termination is valid only on the official cantonal form; the challenge must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority. For those who do not have Swiss citizenship, SEM distinguishes permit L, short-term and valid for up to one year, B, a renewable residence permit, C, a settlement permit generally after ten years of residence or five for UE/AELS citizens, and G for cross-border commuters. These are checks separate from salary, but they affect the overall assessment of an offer in Canton Vaud.

### 2. Read the working conditions Compare the gross salary, weekly hours, holidays, and notice period. The reference is 45 hours for industry, offices, and sales, and 50 in other sectors; minimum holidays are four weeks, five for those under 20. Also note the 14 weeks of maternity leave at 80% via IPG and the two weeks of paternity leave where applicable.
### 3. Separate payslip and insurance Check the indicated items: AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA, and LPP on the coordinated salary, with the brackets provided for age. Keep the LAMal on a separate line: it is mandatory for residents, private, with a per capita premium, and must be stipulated within three months of arrival. If applicable, check for the cantonal premium reduction.
### 4. Link taxes and housing Remember the three tax levels and do not attribute functions belonging to other offices to the UFAS/BSV or UST/BFS: AFC/ESTV concerns IFD and VAT, while cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxes. For housing, verify the deposit, blocked account, and official form if a notice of termination arrives; the contestation period is 30 days.
### 5. Verify status and updates If you are a foreign national, identify the SEM category: L, B, C, or G. Home price, required own funds, mortgage affordability, transfer tax and notarial fees define the scope of the assessment for anyone buying a home in the Canton of Graubünden. Own funds describe the resources to be put into the purchase, while affordability concerns whether the mortgage can be sustained within the budget under consideration. Transfer tax and notarial fees are part of the transaction costs and should not be confused with federal direct, cantonal or municipal tax.
Swiss taxation follows three levels: federal direct tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. For a person resident in Switzerland, LAMal/KVG is mandatory and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival. The premium is per capita: it is not a tax and not a wage contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region, while the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy. In the apprentice's budget, therefore, health insurance must be counted separately from social security deductions. To compare premiums, you can use the tool at cassa malati LAMal.
Taxation also requires a precise distinction. In Switzerland there are three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; municipalities apply a multiplier to cantonal tax. AFC/ESTV is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations are responsible for the cantonal and municipal levels. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AI/LPP, and does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set tax rates.
| Item | How to include it in the comparison | |---|---| | LAMal/KVG | Per-capita premium, separate from salary | | Taxation | Three levels and canton-specific rules | | Social security | AVS/AI/LPP, not to be confused with taxes | | Cost of living | Budget separate from gross pay and deductions |
If the apprenticeship position entails relocation, federal tenancy law, CO Art. 253 et seq., is the same in every canton. The security deposit may not exceed 3 months' rent and must be placed in a blocked account in the tenant's name. The landlord's notice of termination is valid only on the official cantonal form; the challenge must be submitted within 30 days to the conciliation authority. These are items to include in the calculation of costo della vita in Svizzera, without making up unavailable local amounts.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From searching to deciding
The process can be organised with a record for each opportunity, keeping verified data separate from questions that are still open.
### 1. Find the position
Use the job listings as a starting point and collect the sector, stated location, pay, working hours, holidays and reference to vocational baccalaureate arrangements for each offer. Do not turn missing information into an assumption: record it as a question to ask before signing.
### 2. Read the apprenticeship contract
Before accepting, compare the pay with the maximum working time applicable to the sector and with the minimum holidays. Also ask for the contribution items to be clear and for vocational baccalaureate arrangements to be discussed separately from the simple pay amount. The contract should become the basis of the comparison, not a document to consult after making the choice.
### 3. Build the gross-to-net calculation
Enter AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP/BVG on separate lines. For AD/AC, check the annual ceiling instead of replacing it with an outdated figure; for LAINF, consider the sector; for LPP, use the coordinated salary and the stated age bracket. Figures indexed each year must be checked before preparing the budget.
### 4. Check insurance and personal status
If the person is resident, record the three-month deadline for LAMal. For an adult, the deductibles are CHF 300, 500, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 or 2,500; the premium remains per capita and a cantonal reduction may be available. For a foreign applicant, SEM distinguishes the L permit, lasting up to one year, the renewable B permit, the C permit, normally after 10 years of residence or 5 years for EU/EFTA nationals, and the G permit for frontier workers.
### 5. Keep vocational baccalaureate arrangements separate
Give the conditions, organisation and documents to be checked with the contact person their own section. This keeps the training decision readable even when pay, deductions and the cost of living are calculated separately.
To turn these items into an orderly comparison of gross pay, deductions and monthly budget, use the salary calculator.
